answer.rationale: Finance's 18% mandate is non-negotiable this cycle and the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price, eliminating negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent as mandate-compliant options; the contract's non-auto-renewal in 14 days also forecloses defer_decision for this primary, critical line. memory_c2 records a prior successful low-cost-vendor switch (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) which supports switch_primary_vendor as directionally sound, but that record doesn't capture performance under a zero-buffer, 94%-utilized line — a materially different risk context. Given the stated objective explicitly includes not increasing delivery risk, I intend to scale this as a small_guarded_test (e.g., phased/partial cutover with incumbent overlap where possible) rather than a full broad switch, so a qualification failure doesn't propagate into missed committed volume. I want to verify c2's original record for onboarding lead time and any caveats, and c1's record on integration stability to weigh the true switching cost against the mandate. add_second_source (c3) is noted as a strong future risk-mitigation lever but doesn't resolve the imminent contract expiration this cycle, so it's deferred to next review.
